## Add a map

Place `bloomOutput()` in your UI and `renderBloom()` in your server. No separate CSS or JavaScript is needed.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
library(shiny)
library(bloomr)

ui <- fluidPage(
  bloomOutput("map", height = "520px"),
  textOutput("chosen")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$map <- renderBloom({ bloom_map() })

  output$chosen <- renderText({
    req(input$map_selected)
    paste(input$map_selected$name, input$map_selected$level)
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

When someone selects a region, `input$map_selected` gives its `id`, `geoid`, `name`, `level`, and `parent_id`. Use these values to filter another output. Different map IDs keep their selections separate.

## Update the colors without moving the map

Use a proxy when an indicator changes. This updates the values without resetting the current view or dragged positions.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
observeEvent(input$metric, {
  bloom_update_data(
    bloomProxy("map"),
    data = county_data,
    key = "geoid",
    value = input$metric
  )
}, ignoreInit = TRUE)
```

Here `county_data` is a data frame with a character `geoid` column and numeric indicator columns. Put the code inside the Shiny server and provide a `metric` input.

To update hover details at the same time, add `tooltip_fields` to the proxy call:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
bloom_update_data(
  bloomProxy("map"), county_data, value = input$metric,
  tooltip_fields = c("Population" = "population")
)
```

You can also pass `tooltip_data = details` when descriptions are kept in a separate table. If you omit `tooltip_fields`, the current tooltip details remain unchanged.

If the indicator changes, `bloom_update_data()` can also update the legend title and units:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
bloom_update_data(bloomProxy("map"), county_data,
  value = "density", value_label = "Population density",
  value_suffix = " per sq mi")
```

## Adjust bloom size without resetting the map

To enlarge expanded areas or change how far they spread, use the same map proxy:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
bloom_update_bloom(bloomProxy("map"), bloom_scale = 1.5,
                   bloom_spread = 1.25)
```

`bloom_scale = 1` is the original shape size, and `1.6` is 60 percent larger. `bloom_spread` changes spacing rather than size. Existing selections and manually dragged positions are retained. In a Shiny dashboard with sliders, debounce rapid changes to avoid unnecessary layout calculations.

For a complete example with a standard map, an adjustable map, ggplot2 bars and Plotly,
install the optional `ggplot2` and `plotly` packages first, then run:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
shiny::runApp(system.file("examples", "linked-dashboard", package = "bloomr"))
```


## Select or expand a region from Shiny

```{r, eval=FALSE}
bloom_select(bloomProxy("map"), "bergen")
bloom_expand(bloomProxy("map"), "county")
bloom_reset(bloomProxy("map"))
```

To open smaller areas, first select a county, then use `bloom_expand(bloomProxy("map"), "local")`. Proxies act on the displayed map instead of creating a new one.

## Try the complete example

```{r, eval=FALSE}
run_bloom_example()
```

The example includes an indicator selector, geographic selection feedback, and live map updates. The map fits dashboard cards and Shiny tabs; set a height such as `"520px"` to give it enough room.

For labels, colors, boundary lines, and keyboard controls, see [Appearance and keyboard](appearance-and-keyboard.html).
